name: DeNairo Girton Jr.
strengths: Girton reads the quarterback from deep and drives the sideline throw for clean interceptions — true center-field anticipation.
Girton covers hash-to-boundary with long strides and tracks the deep ball over the shoulder without panic.
Girton click-and-closes from off coverage — breaks on intermediate stems and arrives on time at the catch point.
Girton triggers downhill from a deep shell and is willing to finish in the alley when he diagnoses run.
weaknesses: Girton still needs pad-level and wrap consistency on open-field tackles — the 6-1 / 180 frame arrives high before the strength catches up.
comparison: Girton comps to Jessie Bates III — 6-1 / ~190 lean free-safety mold; center-field range, QB eyes, and ball skills over box thump (size-matched to Girton’s 6-1 / 180 frame).
projection: Girton projects as special teams / package snaps Year 1, then compete for every-down free safety — starter upside as a rangy center-fielder who can grow into STAR looks as he adds mass.
schemeFit: Girton fits a length-first safety room that wants a deep-third / alley defender with range and ball production.
insiderNotes: Girton is a rangy 6-1 / 180 Great Mills free-safety mold with center-field range and natural ball skills. Reads the quarterback, covers ground in long strides, and click-and-closes on intermediate stems. Wins with eyes and range before the frame fills — Bates mold, not a box thumper.
